It isolates pure skill effects by removing spurious correlations induced by confounding variables. In NFL analytics, this separates a player's inherent ability from environmental factors like coaching schemes or opponent quality. The tensor formulation naturally accommodates multi-dimensional skill metrics (e.g., pass protection, run blocking, route running) simultaneously. Computationally, it requires accurate causal graphs and high-quality observational data to estimate the necessary conditional expectations. Failure occurs when important confounders are omitted, leading to residual bias that undermines the deconfounding objective.
